annotations.annotation_text: Fraternal archetype "postman" on page 488 ("The Inquest of Yawn"): the opposing sons — Shem the Penman (introvert artist, tree, darkness) and Shaun the Post (extrovert politician, stone, light) — manifest here within the judicial inquest over the prostrate body of Yawn (Shaun), voices of the dead rising through him, HCE's final confession. Their Brunonian dialectic of coinciding opposites propels the chapter's conflict during this Age of Men phase.
sources: Atherton, James S. The Books at the Wake. https://archive.org/details/booksatwake0000athe
Norris, Margot. The Decentered Universe of Finnegans Wake. https://archive.org/details/decentereduniver0000norr

annotations.annotation_text: The Letter motif "midden" on page 488 ("The Inquest of Yawn"): ALP's mysterious document — scratched from the midden by Biddy Doran the Hen — represents the genesis of all writing within the judicial inquest over the prostrate body of Yawn (Shaun), voices of the dead rising through him, HCE's final confession. During this Age of Men phase, the letter functions simultaneously as archaeological artifact, love note, legal deposition, and the text of Finnegans Wake itself.
sources: Bishop, John. Joyce's Book of the Dark. https://archive.org/details/joycesbookofdark0000bish
Deane, Vincent, et al. The Finnegans Wake Notebooks at Buffalo. https://www.brepols.net

annotations.annotation_text: Oneiric dimension "night" on page 488 ("The Inquest of Yawn"): the nocturnal consciousness surfaces within the judicial inquest over the prostrate body of Yawn (Shaun), voices of the dead rising through him, HCE's final confession. During this Age of Men phase, Joyce reconstructs the sleeping body's sensory deprivation — dimmed sight, distorted hearing, dream-logic association — transforming somatic experience into polyphonic language.
sources: Bishop, John. Joyce's Book of the Dark. https://archive.org/details/joycesbookofdark0000bish

annotations.annotation_text: Tavern/jury motif "bottle" on page 488 ("The Inquest of Yawn"): the twelve customers drinking in HCE's Chapelizod pub represent public opinion, the Zodiac, and the Apostles within the judicial inquest over the prostrate body of Yawn (Shaun), voices of the dead rising through him, HCE's final confession. During this Age of Men phase, they judge, condemn, and demand another round — the Greek chorus of middle-class Dublin gossip.
